Fitted Efron log-spline model objects

Source: R/methods.R, R/predict.R, R/format-print.R, and 1 more
bef_fit.Rd

Objects of class c("bef_fit_re", "bef_fit"), as returned by bayes_efron_fit(), contain the posterior draws, the data, the settings of the fit and summaries of the draws (see Details). There are methods for printing and summarizing a fit, for posterior means, intervals and quantiles of the site effects, and for extracting the posterior draws. For plots, predictions, diagnostics and model comparison, see plot.bef_fit_re(), predict.bef_fit_re(), diagnose() and loo.bef_fit().

Usage

# S3 method for class 'bef_fit'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'bef_fit'
summary(object, level = 0.9, ...)

# S3 method for class 'bef_fit_re'
summary(object, level = 0.9, ...)

# S3 method for class 'summary.bef_fit'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'bef_fit_re'
coef(object, type = c("mean", "mode", "map"), ...)

# S3 method for class 'bef_fit_re'
confint(
  object,
  parm = NULL,
  level = 0.9,
  type = c("theta", "g"),
  method = c("exact", "draws"),
  interval = c("equal-tailed", "hpd"),
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'bef_fit_re'
vcov(object, full = FALSE, ...)

# S3 method for class 'bef_fit_re'
fitted(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'bef_fit_re'
as.data.frame(x, row.names = NULL, optional = FALSE, ...)

# S3 method for class 'bef_fit'
nobs(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'bef_fit'
logLik(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'bef_fit'
as_draws(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'bef_fit'
format(x, ..., use_cli = NULL)

# S3 method for class 'bef_fit_re'
quantile(
  x,
  probs = c(0.05, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.95),
  reading = c("interpolated", "step"),
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'summary.bef_fit'
format(x, ..., use_cli = NULL)

# S3 method for class 'bef_fit_re'
residuals(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'bef_fit_re'
simulate(object, nsim = 1, seed = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'bef_fit'
ndraws(x)

# S3 method for class 'bef_fit'
variables(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'bef_fit'
AIC(object, ..., k = 2)

# S3 method for class 'bef_fit'
BIC(object, ...)

Arguments

x, object

A bef_fit object created by bayes_efron_fit(). For the summary.bef_fit methods, the result of summary().

...

Arguments passed on to format() by the print() methods. summary() throws an error if any are supplied; the other methods ignore them.

level

Posterior probability of the intervals, a number between 0 and 1.

type

For coef(), the summary to return: "mean" (the default) for the posterior means or "mode" for the posterior modes ("map", the earlier name of "mode", is also accepted). For confint(), the quantities for which intervals are returned: "theta" (the default) for the site effects or "g" for the mean, variance and standard deviation of \(g\).

parm

The sites or parameters for which confint() returns intervals. For type = "theta", a numeric vector of site positions in the data or a character vector of site labels. For type = "g", one or more of "mean_g", "var_g" and "sd_g", or their positions. If NULL (the default), all are returned.

method

How confint() computes the limits for type = "theta". "exact" (the default) takes them from the posterior distribution of the site effect, which averages over the draws of \(g\). "draws" takes them as sample quantiles of the theta_rep draws and requires a fit made with site_draws = TRUE.

interval

Type of interval returned by confint(). "equal-tailed" (the default) has its limits at the quantiles (1 - level) / 2 and 1 - (1 - level) / 2. "hpd" is the shortest interval with posterior probability level; if the distribution has one mode, it is the highest posterior density interval. For method = "draws" and for type = "g", "hpd" gives the shortest interval that contains at least that proportion of the draws. The two types differ whenever the posterior distribution is not symmetric, and most when it has two modes.

full

If TRUE, vcov() also returns the covariances between sites. If FALSE (the default), the matrix is diagonal.

row.names

Optional character vector of row names for as.data.frame(), one per site.

optional

Not used; it is an argument of the generic.

use_cli

If TRUE and the cli package is installed, the first line of the output is bold and, in a printed summary, the section titles are colored. If FALSE, the output is plain text. If NULL (the default), the value of getOption("bayesEfron.use_cli", TRUE) is used.

probs

Numeric vector of probabilities for quantile(), each greater than 0 and less than 1.

reading

How quantile() computes quantiles from point masses on the grid. "interpolated" (the default) spreads the probability of each grid point evenly over one grid spacing around it, and "step" leaves it on the grid point. See the Details of g_summary().

nsim

Number of joint draws for simulate(), a positive integer.

seed

Integer seed for the draws of simulate(), or NULL (the default) for none. If a seed is given, the state of R's random number generator is restored afterward.

k

Not used.

Value

summary() returns a list of class summary.bef_fit. coef(), fitted() and residuals() return numeric vectors with one element per site. confint() and as.data.frame() return data frames, and vcov(), quantile() and simulate() return matrices. The print() methods return x invisibly. The other methods are described in the two lists below: "Methods (by generic)" for class bef_fit, and "Functions" for class bef_fit_re and for a summary.

Details

A fitted object is a list with the components draws, posterior and metadata, and with cmdstan_fit if the model was fitted with keep_cmdstan_fit = TRUE.

draws is a posterior::draws_array with the posterior draws of the following variables.

  • lp__: The log density of the posterior distribution up to a constant, as reported by CmdStan.

  • alpha: The spline coefficients.

  • lambda: The precision of the prior for the spline coefficients.

  • log_g: The log probabilities of \(g\) at the grid points.

  • mean_g, var_g, sd_g: The mean, variance and standard deviation of \(g\).

  • effective_params: The effective number of parameters defined below.

  • log_marginal_likelihood: The marginal log likelihood of the estimates, with the site effects integrated out.

A fit made with site_draws = TRUE stores five more variables per site.

  • theta_mean, theta_sd, theta_map: The mean, standard deviation and mode of the posterior distribution of \(\theta_i\) given \(g\).

  • theta_rep: A draw from that distribution.

  • log_lik: The log likelihood of the site's estimate.

Otherwise these variables are not stored, and the methods compute the site summaries from the draws of \(g\).

posterior is a list with the draws of mean_g, var_g, sd_g, effective_params and log_marginal_likelihood as numeric vectors.

metadata is a list with the data, the settings of the fit and summaries of the draws. It has the following components.

  • model_family: The model family, currently always "RE".

  • grid_method: The method that chose the limits of the grid, or "support" if the limits were specified directly.

  • seed: The seed used by the sampler.

  • cmdstan_version: The version of CmdStan.

  • stan_file_sha256: The SHA-256 hash of the Stan file.

  • data_list: The data passed to Stan, a list with the estimates theta_hat, the standard errors sigma, the grid points grid, the spline basis B, and the numbers of sites, grid points and spline functions (K, L and M).

  • runtime_seconds: The time taken by sampling, in seconds.

  • theta_summary: The table of site effects, a data frame with one row per site. Its columns are described below.

  • mean_g_summary, var_g_summary, effective_params_summary, log_marginal_likelihood_summary: Lists with the mean, the standard deviation and the 5%, 50% and 95% quantiles of the draws.

More information is stored in attributes of metadata and can be extracted with attr(), e.g., attr(fit$metadata, "grid").

  • sampler_settings: A list with the values of chains, parallel_chains, iter_warmup, iter_sampling, adapt_delta, max_treedepth, seed, refresh and init passed to CmdStan.

  • grid: The grid of the fit, as returned by make_efron_grid(). It can be supplied as grid in another fit.

  • storage: A list recording whether the site-level draws are stored, the number of chains, the number of iterations stored per chain, and the value of thin.

  • package_version, cmdstanr_version: The versions of bayesEfron and cmdstanr used for the fit.

theta_summary, the table of site effects, has the columns listed below. The columns from mean to mode summarize the posterior distribution of \(\theta_i\), which averages over the posterior draws of \(g\) (Lee and Sui, 2025, Section 4.3).

  • site: The site number, in the order of the data.

  • label: The site label, or the site number if the data had no labels.

  • estimate, se: The estimate and its standard error, as supplied.

  • mean: The posterior mean.

  • sd: The posterior standard deviation. The posterior variance is the variance of \(\theta_i\) given \(g\), averaged over the draws of \(g\), plus the variance over those draws of the mean of \(\theta_i\) given \(g\), so sd includes the uncertainty about \(g\).

  • lower, upper: The 5% and 95% quantiles of the posterior distribution, i.e., the limits of an equal-tailed 90% interval. They are quantiles of the distribution itself and not sample quantiles of site-level draws. For a fit with point masses they are computed with the "interpolated" reading (described under reading), so they generally fall between grid points.

  • mode: The posterior mode. For point masses this is the grid point with the largest posterior probability, and for normal components the value at which the posterior density is largest.

  • hpdi_lower, hpdi_upper, map: Deprecated columns that repeat lower, upper and mode. They will be removed.

Like all site summaries, the posterior summaries in this table are computed from the stored draws of \(g\) and are subject to the Monte Carlo error of those draws. site_summary() returns the same table for any level, with additional columns.

effective_params is the sum over sites of the ratio of the posterior variance of \(\theta_i\) given \(g\) to \(\sigma_i^2\). In the normal random-effects model this ratio is the weight given to the site's own estimate, so the sum is small when the estimates are shrunk strongly and close to the number of sites when there is little shrinkage. Note that p_loo in loo.bef_fit(), which the loo package also calls the effective number of parameters, is a different quantity.

In the printed summary, the mean, variance and standard deviation of \(g\) are labeled "Prior g", because \(g\) is the prior distribution of each \(\theta_i\).

A fit saved by an earlier version of the package may contain a table of site effects or a value of effective_params computed under other definitions. The methods then recompute them from the stored draws of \(g\) and issue a warning that names the recomputed quantities. The saved object is not changed.

Methods (by generic)

  • print(bef_fit): Prints the number of sites, the number of draws, the worst value of each sampler diagnostic, the range of the standard errors, the grid and the method that chose its range, and the functions to call next.

  • summary(bef_fit): Returns a list of class summary.bef_fit with the components prior_summary (the posterior means of the mean, variance and standard deviation of \(g\)) and diagnostics (the sampler diagnostics; see diagnose()).

  • nobs(bef_fit): Returns the number of sites.

  • logLik(bef_fit): Returns the posterior mean of log_marginal_likelihood, the marginal log likelihood with the site effects integrated out, as a logLik object. Its degrees of freedom are the posterior mean of effective_params. Note that this is not a maximized log likelihood, so AIC() and BIC() throw an error. Use loo.bef_fit() to compare fits.

  • as_draws(bef_fit): Returns the posterior draws as a posterior::draws_array.

  • format(bef_fit): Returns the lines that print() shows as a character vector.

  • ndraws(bef_fit): Returns the number of posterior draws stored in the fit, summed over the chains.

  • variables(bef_fit): Returns the names of the variables in the draws.

  • AIC(bef_fit): AIC() and BIC() throw an error, for the reason given under logLik().

Functions

  • summary(bef_fit_re): Adds the component theta_summary to the summary: the table of site effects described in Details, with equal-tailed intervals at level.

  • print(summary.bef_fit): Prints the summary.

  • coef(bef_fit_re): Returns the posterior means or the posterior modes of the site effects (the column mean or mode of theta_summary) as a numeric vector. Its names are the site labels, or the site numbers if the data had no labels.

  • confint(bef_fit_re): Returns a data frame of posterior intervals with the attribute level. For type = "theta" it has one row per site and the columns site, mean, lower and upper. For type = "g" it has one row each for the mean, variance and standard deviation of \(g\) and the columns parameter, mean, lower and upper. The limits are computed as specified by method and interval. The column point and, for type = "g", the column site repeat mean and parameter. They are deprecated and will be removed.

  • vcov(bef_fit_re): Returns the posterior variances of the site effects (the squares of the column sd of theta_summary) as a diagonal matrix. If full = TRUE, the matrix also contains the posterior covariances between sites. The site effects are independent given \(g\) but not in the posterior distribution, because all of them depend on \(g\). Their covariances are the covariances, over the draws of \(g\), of the means of the effects given \(g\). The diagonal matrix is sufficient when sites are considered one at a time. Use full = TRUE for the variance of a sum or a difference of site effects.

  • fitted(bef_fit_re): Returns the posterior means of the site effects, as coef(object) does.

  • as.data.frame(bef_fit_re): Returns theta_summary, the table of site effects described in Details, with 90% intervals.

  • quantile(bef_fit_re): Returns quantiles of the posterior distributions of the site effects as a matrix with one row per site and one column per probability in probs.

  • format(summary.bef_fit): Returns the lines of the printed summary as a character vector.

  • residuals(bef_fit_re): Returns the estimates minus the posterior means of the site effects, as a numeric vector named by the site labels.

  • simulate(bef_fit_re): Draws the site effects jointly from their posterior distribution. For each of the nsim draws, one posterior draw of \(g\) is taken and every site effect is drawn from its distribution given that \(g\). Returns a matrix with one row per draw and one column per site. Each row is one joint draw, so functions of several sites (e.g., ranks or the largest effect) can be computed row by row.

References

Lee, J. and Sui, D. (2025). Fully Bayesian inference for meta-analytic deconvolution using Efron's log-spline prior. Mathematics, 13(16), 2639. doi:10.3390/math13162639

See also

bayes_efron_fit(), diagnose(), plot.bef_fit_re(), predict.bef_fit_re(), loo.bef_fit()

Examples

fit <- krw_fit
fit
#> <bayesEfron fit>
#> Model family: RE
#> Sites: 97
#> Grid method: pilot
#> Runtime: 0.7197 sec
#> Draws: 800 (4 chains, one iteration in 15 kept); site-level draws not kept
#> Diagnostics: Rhat 1.002; ESS bulk 1731; ESS tail 1780; divergences 0; treedepth hits 0
#> Standard errors: 0.005344 to 0.0392 (largest / smallest 7.335)
#> Grid: 101 points from -0.0829 to 0.1585; smallest standard error 2.213 grid spacings
#> Grid range: rule "pilot", not narrowed (the range of "paper_realdata"); point masses; 6 spline functions
#> Next: summary() and site_summary() for the sites, g_summary() for the distribution of effects, plot().
summary(fit)$prior_summary
#> $mean
#> [1] 0.01660178
#> 
#> $var
#> [1] 0.0003076948
#> 
#> $sd
#> [1] 0.01716216
#> 

# Posterior means, next to the estimates they are shrunk from.
head(cbind(estimate = krw_discrimination$yi, posterior_mean = coef(fit)))
#>                        estimate posterior_mean
#> Rite Aid            0.046957123    0.030481747
#> KFC                 0.022000000    0.017864935
#> Victoria's Secret   0.042161613    0.023347817
#> United Rentals      0.005708306    0.010719906
#> Cardinal Health     0.034077110    0.021096229
#> Charter / Spectrum -0.010182468    0.001675308

# Intervals for three sites, and for the mean and spread of g.
confint(fit, parm = c(29, 11, 65), level = 0.95)
#> 95% posterior intervals (equal-tailed)
#>                   site         mean        lower       upper        point
#> Quest Diagnostics   29 -0.004794688 -0.014809407 0.004878364 -0.004794688
#> J.C. Penney         11  0.021602438  0.001058169 0.045289468  0.021602438
#> Walmart             65  0.023868227 -0.003405634 0.065165090  0.023868227
confint(fit, type = "g")
#> 90% posterior intervals (equal-tailed)
#>   parameter         mean        lower        upper   site        point
#> 1    mean_g 0.0166017761 0.0130811925 0.0206491286 mean_g 0.0166017761
#> 2     var_g 0.0003076948 0.0001399332 0.0005738865  var_g 0.0003076948
#> 3      sd_g 0.0171621568 0.0118293270 0.0239559271   sd_g 0.0171621568

# Posterior standard deviations and posterior modes, with the standard
# errors of the estimates.
head(cbind(se = krw_discrimination$sei, as.data.frame(fit)[c("mean", "sd", "mode")]))
#>           se        mean          sd        mode
#> 1 0.01619358 0.030481747 0.012967949 0.028158038
#> 2 0.01530472 0.017864935 0.010525940 0.016086924
#> 3 0.02296031 0.023347817 0.013848996 0.020915369
#> 4 0.01504751 0.010719906 0.009844949 0.008844255
#> 5 0.02145421 0.021096229 0.012896169 0.018501147
#> 6 0.01209059 0.001675308 0.008784082 0.001601586

# Posterior variances as a diagonal matrix.
diag(vcov(fit))[1:3]
#>          Rite Aid               KFC Victoria's Secret 
#>      0.0001681677      0.0001107954      0.0001917947
